 Second round of November Social Security payments goes out in 7 days
 By Mackenzie Chase 
 Published
 November 11, 2026 6:00am ET
 Advertisement -->
 Advertisement 
 Add Washington Examiner on Google
 Advertisement 
 The second round of November Social Security payments for retirees, now capped at $5,181, will be issued in seven days.
 When will payments arrive?
 The second round will go out on Wednesday, Nov. 18, to those born between the 11th and 20th of a month.

 The first round went out on Tuesday , Nov. 10, to retirees born on or before the 10th of a month, and the third round will go out on Nov. 25 to those born on or after the 21st of a month.
 Advertisement 
 Who is eligible?
 Citizens are eligible for Social Security payments beginning at age 62.
 How much will I receive?
 Payments are largely reliant on a person’s retirement age. While the youngest retiring age, 62, could receive up to $2,969 per month, a recipient who waited until 70 years old could receive up to $5,181 per month, according to the Social Security Administration.
 For those who wait until full retirement age, their benefit would be up to $4,152. Anyone born in 1960 or later must be 67 years old to be considered full retirement age, according to the Social Security Administration. 
 Advertisement The benefit could be less if the recipient earned less than the taxable maximum.
 TREASURY ANNOUNCES DEFICIT ROSE TO $1.99 TRILLION IN FISCAL 2026 
 Beneficiaries can see a personalized estimate of how much they could expect each month using the SSA’s calculator .
 Advertisement How is it financed?
 Employers and employees finance the Social Security fund through withholdings.
 However, payment amounts could change unless Congress takes action to address the depleting fund. According to a report from trustees, the retirement fund is set to run out by 2032 due to a rising number of retirees and a shrinking workforce.
